clue.text: National currency exists to protect society in depression

indicators.note: to protect means the word society's letter is held within the other pieces

parts.note: the euro is the single currency of much of Europe
exists means is, as in 'there is'

explanation.surface: A nation's money crisis drags the whole of society into economic depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks economic beside currency, but it is the mental sense; 'to protect' wraps the currency and 'exists' round the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental disorder, and depression is one such psychological condition.

clue.text: For ever on the outside, having dropped by

indicators.note: having dropped says a letter is lost from the longer word

parts.note: on the outside means external, exterior
by as in 'three by four' is the multiplication sign X

explanation.surface: Someone standing outside forever, having merely dropped by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having dropped' removes X (the times sign, read from 'by') from EXTERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal lasts without end, which is the meaning of for ever.

clue.text: Could Axis be very American?

parts.note: could means might, as in 'it might rain'
Y is a mathematical axis on a graph

explanation.surface: A wartime question: could the Axis powers be very American?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axis' calls up the wartime alliance, but here it is the y-axis of a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: In American informal speech mighty is an intensifier meaning extremely, as in 'mighty fine'.

clue.text: Agency's top property wants one to quit

indicators.note: to quit says the named letter leaves the word

parts.note: wants means desires
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An estate agency's best house is going because a resident wants to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: DES RES is estate-agent shorthand for a desirable residence, a house they talk up.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate agents advertise their best homes as a desirable residence, shortened in listings.

clue.text: Piles here in behind, round middle of rectum hole

indicators.note: round says the rear's letters go around the other pieces

parts.note: behind means the rear, the backside

indicators.note: middle of takes the central pair of letters of the word rectum

parts.note: O is a hole by its shape

explanation.surface: A crude medical joke about haemorrhoids and the back passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piles' looks like haemorrhoids, matching the surface, but an atomic pile was an early name for a nuclear reactor; 'round' wraps the rear about the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Early nuclear reactors were called atomic piles, so piles are found in this machine.

clue.text: Guy at mouth of "silvery" river

indicators.note: at mouth of picks the opening letter of the word silvery

parts.note: the Tay is a river in Scotland, called 'silvery Tay' in a famous bad poem

explanation.surface: A man stands where a silvery river meets the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is Scotland's longest river; 'Guy' is not a man but a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy rope holding a mast or tent steady is also called a stay.

clue.text: I'm fully alert at first in inconclusive test for drink

indicators.note: in places the expanded words inside the shortened test
inconclusive says the word lacks its last letter, its conclusion

parts.note: a trial is a test
I'm written out in full is I am

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word alert

explanation.surface: Someone insists they are sober after a failed breath test for drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inconclusive' cuts TRIAL to TRIA; 'in' puts I AM plus A inside it after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a coffee liqueur, a brand of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Citing as evidence acid dug up with note

indicators.note: up as in 'churned up' signals the letters are mixed

parts.note: N is short for note, as in banknote abbreviations

explanation.surface: An analyst cites acid dug up on a site, with a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' shuffles ACID, DUG and N together.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce is to put forward a fact or example as proof in an argument.

clue.text: A coalition member's one excuse to get off

parts.note: a Lib, a Liberal Democrat, was a member of the 2010 UK coalition government
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A junior partner in government offers an excuse to escape blame.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats were junior partners in the UK coalition of 2010-15.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere that lets a suspect get off a charge.

clue.text: Occasionally strike match

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter of the word strike

explanation.surface: Every so often a match fails to strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike match' suggests lighting up, but match here means a draw or pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie is to equal or be level with, which is one sense of match.

clue.text: Time to arrest traitor for his mistakes

indicators.note: to arrest means to hold, so the time word holds the traitor

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a traitor or informer

explanation.surface: It is time to arrest the traitor for his crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is a list of corrections for printing errors in a book.

clue.text: District where Tory's led quivering inside?

indicators.note: inside puts the shaken letters within the political wing word

parts.note: the Tories are the party of the right

indicators.note: quivering suggests the letters of led shaking into a new order

explanation.surface: A Tory MP is led trembling into a seedy part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer comes before 'District' to name the area where prostitutes work. 'quivering' gives EDL from the clue's own word, and 'inside' sets it within the political wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-light district is the part of a city known for brothels and sex work.

clue.text: Take exam primarily to get a place

parts.note: to sit an exam is to take it

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word exam

explanation.surface: Pass the entrance test to get a place at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location, the spot where something is.

clue.text: One female in torn scanty clothing free of sin?

indicators.note: clothing means the reordered letters cover the other pieces
torn signals the letters of scanty ripped into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A woman in ripped, skimpy clothes is hardly free of sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' gives SANCTY from scanty; 'clothing' puts I and F inside it before the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanctify is to make holy, purifying someone from wrongdoing; the question mark marks the verb sense.

clue.text: Are its origins in fowl leaving Ukraine?

definitions.text: Are its origins in fowl leaving Ukraine?

indicators.note: origins in takes the first letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Did the bird disease start in poultry from Ukraine?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: bird flu begins in fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird flu, an influenza virus, spreads among poultry before reaching people.

clue.text: Qualifier fails miserably to win in tight finish

indicators.note: to win means to take in, so the jumbled letters take in the next word
miserably signals the letters of fails are wretchedly jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finish picks the last letter of the word tight

explanation.surface: An athlete fails badly to win in a close finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miserably' gives FALIS from fails; 'to win' puts IN inside it after F, and T ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: A finalist has qualified for the final round of a competition.

clue.text: Artist atomised compressed water

indicators.note: atomised means broken into pieces, so the letters of artist are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist sprays water from an atomiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow channel of sea, squeezed between two coasts.

clue.text: Wilson's misquoted assurance corrected in UK, once he'd opportunity

indicators.note: corrected says the following words are put into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving its letters

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister's famous promise, misquoted, is put right now that he has a chance.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1967 Harold Wilson, UK Prime Minister, said devaluation did not mean the money in people's pockets lost value; the line is usually misquoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilson's 1967 devaluation broadcast is remembered by a phrase reassuring Britons their savings were safe.

clue.text: See 18 Down
In deep water I can cope with problems if pressure falls

indicators.note: with problems suggests the remaining letters are disordered
falls means the letter drops out of the phrase

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A diver insists they can cope at depth unless the pressure drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In deep water' suggests trouble, but here it is literal. 'falls' removes P from I CAN COPE, and 'with problems' jumbles ICANCOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanic means belonging to the open sea, where the water is deepest.

clue.text: Peter has falsified criminal record

indicators.note: falsified means faked or altered, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Peter has faked his criminal history.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap sheet is American slang for a police file listing someone's arrests.

clue.text: Dread going bust having admitted, say, lower quality

indicators.note: having admitted means letting something inside
going bust means collapsing, so the letters of dread are broken up

parts.note: say is for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A firm fears bankruptcy after admitting it cut product quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going bust' gives DRADE from dread; 'having admitted' puts EG inside after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade something is to reduce its standard or worth.

clue.text: Harry, desperate to release son, went over again

indicators.note: Harry as a verb means harass, so the letters are disturbed
to release means to let go, so the letter leaves the word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: Prince Harry, desperate to free his son, went over the same ground again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the prince but is the verb meaning harass, the anagram signal. 'to release' drops S from desperate, leaving DEPERATE to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated means did once more, as when going over something again.

clue.text: They get this number across in short nursery ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken and rearranged
short says the word nursery loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Children run around a small nursery playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this number across' is clue 23 across, REPEATED: reruns are programmes that get repeated. 'short' cuts nursery to NURSER; 'ground' shuffles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reruns are broadcasts shown a second time, so they are what gets repeated.

clue.text: See 18
Some play El Paso (the old record) in part of Barking

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A DJ plays the old record El Paso while the dogs bark.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took the definition as 'the old record) in part of Barking'; the definition is just 'part of Barking'. The bracket is a second route: the old 'the' is YE, a record is LP.
explanation.definitionFit: A yelp is a sharp cry, the kind of sound a dog makes when barking.

clue.text: If this cut's 23A it's fast

definitions.meaning: said twice, as an urgent call, the word means quickly, hurry up

explanation.surface: A butcher's cut, done twice, is done quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 23A is REPEATED: the word said twice is the cry for speed, 'chop-chop'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chop is a cutting stroke; doubled, chop-chop is slang for hurry up.

clue.text: He may describe his job as ideal on radio

definitions.text: He may describe his job as ideal on radio

parts.words: He may describe his job as ideal on radio
parts.note: the word ideal, said out loud, sounds like 'I deal', which a casino worker who hands out cards could say of his work

explanation.surface: A man on the radio says his job is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'ideal' is 'I deal': the casino worker who deals cards and runs the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier runs a casino gaming table, dealing cards and taking bets.

clue.text: Island's hard on footwear, some say

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: some say means the word is how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a shoe is a piece of footwear

explanation.surface: Life on the island is hard on shoes, some claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Honshu is the largest of the islands of Japan, where Tokyo stands.

clue.text: One opposite to 12 in the past

parts.note: one is the article a
the opposite of a red light, clue 12, is a green signal meaning go

explanation.surface: Something on the far side of the red-light district was in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is RED LIGHT; its opposite at traffic lights is go.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means before now, back in time.

clue.text: Like 1, team takes heed, rejecting odds

indicators.note: takes means the team word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: United is a common football team name, such as Manchester United

indicators.note: rejecting odds keeps only the even letters of the word heed

explanation.surface: A team pays attention but throws out the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting odds' keeps the second and fourth letters of heed; 'takes' sets them inside the team after its first two letters. '1' refers to clue 1, which shares this quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Unedited means left raw and uncorrected, the quality the cross-referenced clue describes.
